title: How training makes you fitter
examples: What is the main job of my heart when I exercise?
How does my body get stronger from training?
If I train too much, what happens to my muscles?

explain.say: Today we learn how training makes your body fitter.
Your heart and lungs work together to give you oxygen.
When you exercise your heart pumps faster to move oxygen.
Your muscles get stronger because they adapt to the work.
Muscles need time to repair and get ready for more work.
When you play a long sport like soccer, you need all these things.

faq.q: Why do I feel tired after running?
faq.a: You feel tired because your muscles have used up much of their energy stores. Your body needs time to refill these stores and repair tiny tears in the muscle fibres.
asks: Why do I feel worn out?

faq.q: Does my heart get bigger from training?
faq.a: Your heart becomes more efficient, meaning it can pump more blood with fewer beats. It does not necessarily get physically bigger, but it gets stronger.
asks: How does training help my heart?

faq.q: What is adaptation in the body?
faq.a: Adaptation means your body changes slightly to cope better with repeated stress. If you keep training, your body adapts to be fitter.

faq.q: Is it okay to train every single day?
faq.a: No, you need rest days. Rest allows your muscles to repair themselves fully. Training without rest can lead to injury or overtraining.
asks: Should I rest when I train?
How much rest do I need?

faq.q: What is the link between my lungs and my muscles?
faq.a: Your lungs provide the oxygen that your blood carries to your working muscles. The muscles use that oxygen to create energy for movement.
asks: Do my lungs power my muscles?
What do lungs give to muscles?

facts: The heart pumps blood containing oxygen around the body.
Muscles adapt by becoming stronger and more efficient with regular exercise.
Resting allows the body time to repair muscle fibres damaged during activity.
Breathing deeply increases the amount of oxygen available to the bloodstream.

quiz.say: During intense exercise, what system works hardest to supply oxygen?
quiz.why: The heart pumps blood and the lungs take in oxygen, so both work together.

wrong.1: This system helps you get energy from food, but it does not directly supply oxygen.
wrong.2: The bones provide support, but they do not manage the oxygen supply.
wrong.3: This system sends signals, but it does not carry the oxygen itself.

quiz.say: If you train a muscle group repeatedly, what is the main result?

options.show: The muscle will only work when rested
options.say: The muscle will only work when rested

options.show: The muscle will become less flexible
options.say: The muscle will become less flexible

options.show: The muscle will get bigger immediately
options.say: The muscle will get bigger immediately

quiz.why: Adaptation means the muscle gets better and stronger at the task it is asked to do.

wrong.0: Muscles need work to adapt; they do not only work when they are completely still.
wrong.1: Training can improve flexibility, but the primary result is strength, not stiffness.
wrong.3: While it gets stronger, the change is gradual and requires time, not instant growth.

quiz.say: Why is taking a rest day important after a hard training session?

options.show: To allow muscle fibres to repair themselves
options.say: To allow muscle fibres to repair themselves

options.show: Because your heart needs to stop beating
options.say: Because your heart needs to stop beating

options.show: To prevent you from feeling hungry
options.say: To prevent you from feeling hungry

options.show: Because your lungs get tired too
options.say: Because your lungs get tired too

quiz.why: Rest is when the body fixes the small damage from exercise, making you stronger next time.

wrong.1: Your heart never stops beating, even when you are resting; it just beats slower.
wrong.2: Resting helps your muscles, but it does not directly control your feeling of hunger.
wrong.3: Your lungs are very resilient and do not get 'tired' in the same way muscles do.
